title: Tibo's 15 startup truths: talk to users, ship fast, charge more, execute
summary: Tibo, who built Tweet Hunter and Taplio (sold $8m), lists 15 blunt lessons about building a business. The throughline is action over information: talk to users, cut features, ship many products, launch embarrassing V1s, charge more, and ignore ego, courses and fear of competition.

principles.text: Talk to far more users before coding; assumptions are what kill products.
principles.quote: Every successful product I've built started with dozens of conversations. Every failure started with assumptions.

principles.text: Subtract features: fewer, better ones beat a bloated product.
principles.quote: I've never seen a product fail because it did too few things well. I've seen hundreds fail because they did too many things poorly.

principles.text: Ship volume: launch many products because luck comes from repetitions, not coding more.
principles.quote: I launched 10+ products before finding winners. Most people launch 1-2 then quit.

principles.text: Use affiliate programs to amplify existing traction, not to rescue a failing product.
principles.quote: Outrank's affiliate program works because the product already had traction. We amplified existing momentum, we didn't manufacture it from nothing.

principles.text: Competition validates demand; execution speed, marketing and iteration are the real differentiators.
principles.quote: "Someone's already doing this" is a validation signal, not a stop sign.

principles.text: Raise prices: higher prices attract better customers and can lift revenue while lowering churn.
principles.quote: I raised Tweet Hunter prices 5x and revenue doubled while churn decreased. Higher prices attract better customers.
